To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of comments during the first 24 hours after publication can be successfully used to predict the popularity of articles, with a correlation of 0.8, and the prediction accuracy is improved when the number of comments is aggregated over the first 24 and 48 hours after publication, with a correlation reaching 0.9.
the prediction accuracy of a linear regression model for the number of comments in the first hour after publication is 0.85, while for the number of clicks it is 0.65.
the prediction accuracy of our model is 0.75 for the top-100 articles, 0.64 for the top-1,000 articles, 0,56 for the top-10,000 articles and 0.51 for the top-50,000 articles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can we exploit early user activity to predict the popularity of an online article?
the problem of predicting the popularity of online news articles based on the number of user comments during a short period of time after publication.

the following questions: How many user comments are needed for an early prediction? How accurate is the prediction based on the number of users who comment? How do the prediction accuracy and the number of comments needed depend on the popularity of the articles?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the number of users comments is a very good predictor of the expected popularity of online articles.
our proposed model is able to provide a good prediction for the popularity of an article based on early user comments.
the number of comments during the observation period is a good predictor of the final popularity of an article.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of comments in the first 24 hours after publication can be a good proxy for the expected popularity of the article.
we have shown that it is possible to predict the popularity of online news articles with a high accuracy based on early user participation.
the number of users’ comments in a short period of time after publication is a good indicator of the expected popularity of online articles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the number of comments is a good indicator for the popularity of an article, but it is also a good indicator for its unpopularity.
a simple linear model is able to predict the popularity of articles with high accuracy and can be used to provide valuable insights for content providers.

, while predicting the future popularity of articles is still challenging, the proposed model provides a simple and effective way to predict the relative popularity of articles, i.e., the rank of articles among their peers.
